name: Atharva Poly-Plast Ltd
title: Atharva Poly-Plast Ltd - 544812 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Engineering-led polymer molder at 67% utilisation with 88% target and no capex until FY28-29; H1 revenue +77.5% YoY but EBITDA margin 20.3% vs 11.5% in H2, with management blaming a one-month polymer pass-through lag.

summary.headline: H1 FY27 revenue rose 77.5% YoY to INR36.69 crores, while EBITDA margin fell to 20.3% on a raw-material pass-through lag.
summary.overview: H1 FY27 revenue from operations was INR36.69 crores versus INR20.67 crores in H1 FY26 (up 77.5% YoY, up 8.8% HoH). EBITDA rose to INR7.45 crores from INR3.88 crores in H2 FY26, with margin at 20.3% against 11.5% in H2 FY26 and 20.7% for full-year FY26. PAT rose to INR4.38 crores from INR1.75 crores. Management attributed the lower margin versus H1 FY26 to a one-month lag in customer raw-material pass-through as polymer prices spiked in September. Net worth rose to INR46.06 crores post-IPO and borrowings fell 53%, leaving debt-to-equity at 0.1x.

financial_highlights.value: Premium office furniture 53.4%; home appliances 26.9%; engineering solutions and other 19.7%

segments.name: Premium office furniture
segments.commentary: Largest vertical at 53.4% of H1 FY27 revenue; supplies seating components (back frames, seat bases, armrests, star bases, headrests) to Herman Miller, Steelcase, Haworth and Kokuyo. Management said it would be stronger in H2.

segments.name: Home appliance resin
segments.commentary: 26.9% of H1 FY27 revenue (about 30% in H2 FY26), serving Godrej and Vasantha for refrigerators, ACs and hair dryers. Described as a stable volume base.

segments.name: Engineering solutions and other applications
segments.commentary: 19.7% of H1 FY27 revenue (about 22% per management's H1 remark); management guided 22% to 25% of FY27 revenue. In-house engineering services carry very high margins; outsourced production mold development carries lower margins.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue mix guided at about 53% premium furniture, about 26% home appliances and 22% to 25% engineering.
Management expects H2 FY27 to be stronger in premium furniture and engineering services, plus the deferred price recovery from September.
Capacity utilisation targeted at 88% (operational efficiency ceiling), expected around FY28 with capacity growth of about 25%.
Further machine additions expected in FY28-FY29, one machine at a time as utilisation approaches 88%.
Management said it is not chasing growth at any cost and will focus on profitability and engineering capability.
Vinod's question on a 50% growth outlook was answered with a clarification that FY28-29 is when capacity additions come; no explicit FY27 growth figure was restated.
capex_capacity: Plant running at about 67% capacity utilisation (Vinod said about 70%), with headroom to 88% efficiency without new building infrastructure.
Facility: 5.5-acre land parcel, about 40,000 sq ft built-up area, 20 molding machines of 100 to 1,000 tonne clamping force.
Machine addition lead time: 45 to 60 days at most for an injection molding machine; generic 350 to 450 tonne machines available to install in about 15 days.

Drip irrigation co-design project (for a US-based MNC, reported as Toro): pilot mold approved; customer funds molds and assembly machines; company invests in plastic molding machines, testing equipment and a clean manufacturing setup. Flow testing to be done in-house; LSR molding to be imported.
Landholding offers scope for future capacity expansion.
demand_pricing: Polymer prices rose about 22% against a roughly 20% rise in crude; customer contracts pass through 100% of raw material price changes with a one-month lag based on the previous month's average.
About INR1.45 crores of higher-priced billing was raised in October 2026 to recover September polymer increases; management expects these adjustments to even out over the year.
Management said customers are unlikely to add second suppliers because the company engages from the design stage, with programme lifecycles of 8 to 10 years.
Engineering services carry EBITDA margins of over 50%, sometimes 60% to 65%, while outsourced production mold development carries lower margins.
H2 FY26 margin dip was attributed to mix: home appliances about 30% of H2 revenue and fewer high-margin engineering services billings.

qa_highlights.question: Is there additional billing for already-shipped material to recover the margin hit, or will recovery come only in subsequent orders?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the crude rise of about 20% lifted polymer about 22%; pass-through contracts reset with a one-month lag. About INR1.45 crores of higher prices was billed in October, and adjustments are expected to even out over the year.

qa_highlights.question: What is peak capacity utilisation and when will expansion be needed?
qa_highlights.answer: Target operating efficiency is 88%, with no hurdles scaling from 67% to 88%. Management expects to reach 88% around FY28 and then add machines one at a time, with investment in FY28-29.

qa_highlights.question: Will customers add other suppliers as new OEMs enter India, and how fast can capacity scale?
qa_highlights.answer: Customers are unlikely to add suppliers because the company works from design stage. Machine additions take 45 to 60 days, with generic machines installed in about 15 days; scaling is limited by product qualification and forecasts, not buildings.

qa_highlights.question: Why did H2 FY26 margins fall so sharply versus H1 FY26, and will margins be lumpy?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to mix: home appliances were about 30% of H2 FY26 revenue, while H1 had high-margin engineering services billings (about 22%). Management expects a more stable full-year profile with a stronger H2 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the engineering revenue contribution target and what are the other engineering markets?
qa_highlights.answer: Engineering is guided at 22% to 25% of FY27 revenue. Co-design work includes the drip irrigation project, which may later be separated as its own vertical with higher margins.

risks_watch: Raw-material pass-through lag: margins depend on one-month recovery of polymer price moves; a falling price cycle could reverse the benefit.
Margin lumpiness from the mix between in-house engineering services and outsourced mold development; H2 FY26 margin fell to 11.5%.
Drip irrigation co-design project: production timing not stated; success depends on customer qualification and testing cycles.
Customer concentration: Godrej and Vasantha in appliances; global OEMs in premium furniture.
Management's FY27 growth outlook was not stated numerically; the 50% growth reference was not confirmed on the call.
Watch H2 FY27 for whether the one-month pass-through catch-up and premium furniture growth lift margins.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth and balance sheet, and openly defensive on margins, which it attributes to a timing lag and mix. Answers on capacity and the drip irrigation project were specific, but no FY27 growth number was given.
key_quotes: So these are not margins lost, but just a lag in the recovery.
We don't want to chase growth at any cost.

growth.why: Management guides 25% capacity growth in FY28 (machines added FY28-29) with utilisation at 67% and 88% target, and FY27 engineering mix at 22-25% plus H2 premium furniture strength; no explicit FY27 revenue growth figure was restated, and the Q2 standalone growth was not separately stated.

rows.label: Margin expansion

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Utilisation is about 67% against an 88% target, and management plans to reach 88% around FY28 and grow capacity about 25%, with machines added one at a time in FY28-29.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management expects H2 FY27 to be stronger in premium office furniture (53.4% of H1 revenue) and engineering services, but gave no numerical FY27 volume or revenue growth figure.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is only about 67%, below the 80%+ level that usually forces a new capex call, so a machine-by-machine plan is more likely than a new plant announcement before FY28.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: No numerical FY27 growth guidance was restated, and management said it is not chasing growth at any cost, so an upgrade is not signalled.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: A falling polymer price cycle could reverse the one-month pass-through benefit, and H2 FY26 margin already fell to 11.5%.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: A drip irrigation co-design project (pilot mold approved, reported as Toro) could later become its own higher-margin vertical, but production timing was not stated.

rows.label: Drip irrigation co-design for US MNC (reported as Toro)
rows.why: Pilot mold approved and customer funds molds, but production timing is not stated and success depends on customer qualification and testing cycles.

rows.label: Pass-through price recovery from September polymer spike
rows.why: About INR1.45 crores of higher-priced billing was raised in October 2026 and management expects adjustments to even out over the year.

rows.label: Engineering services mix lift
rows.why: Engineering is guided at 22-25% of FY27 revenue versus about 19.7% in H1, and in-house engineering carries over 50% EBITDA margins.
